chordInfo.name: Add Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Discover the shimmery, open sound of add chords - enriched triads that add color tones without the complexity of seventh chords.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Triads with an added tone (9th, 11th, or 2nd) but NO 7th degree

fundamentals.label: Formula (add9)
fundamentals.value: Root + Major 3rd + Perfect 5th + Major 9th (same as 2nd, up an octave)

fundamentals.label: Formula (add11)
fundamentals.value: Root + Major 3rd + Perfect 5th + Perfect 11th (same as 4th, up an octave)

fundamentals.label: Key Distinction
fundamentals.value: Unlike 9th chords, add chords omit the 7th - Cadd9 (C-E-G-D) vs C9 (C-E-G-Bb-D)

fundamentals.label: Sound Quality
fundamentals.value: Open, shimmery, bright - richer than a triad but cleaner than extended chords

applications.label: Acoustic Pop/Rock
applications.value: Staple of Oasis, Coldplay, U2, and modern singer-songwriters

applications.label: Worship & Ambient
applications.value: Open ringing voicings create wide, atmospheric textures

applications.label: Folk & Country
applications.value: Fingerpicked add9 arpeggios for gentle, colorful accompaniment

applications.label: Indie & Alternative
applications.value: Replacing plain major chords for a more sophisticated, dreamy feel

boxes.title: Cadd9 Example
items: Root: C (1st degree)
Major 3rd: E (3rd degree)
Perfect 5th: G (5th degree)
Major 9th: D (2nd/9th degree)
Result: C-E-G-D (no B, no 7th)

boxes.title: Add vs Extended Chords
items: Cadd9 = C-E-G-D (triad + 9th, no 7th)
C9 = C-E-G-Bb-D (dominant 7th + 9th)
Cmaj9 = C-E-G-B-D (major 7th + 9th)
Add chords are simpler: just a triad plus one note
The missing 7th keeps the sound clean and open

boxes.title: Variations & Naming
items: add9: Most common - triad plus the 9th (= 2nd up an octave)
add2: Same pitches as add9, but 2nd placed close to root
add11: Triad plus the 11th (= 4th up an octave)
add(#11): Triad plus raised 11th for Lydian color
Minor add9: Minor triad + 9th (e.g., Cm(add9) = C-Eb-G-D)

voicingGroups.title: Essential Open Add Chord Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These open-position add9 shapes are among the most used chords in modern guitar. Many require just one extra finger added to a familiar shape.

voicings.name: Cadd9
voicings.fingering: Based on open C shape, lift pinky to open 3rd string
voicings.use: Extremely common in pop/rock, pairs with G and D

voicings.name: Gadd9
voicings.fingering: Open G shape with 2nd fret on 1st string
voicings.use: Classic acoustic voicing, Oasis and Wonderwall staple

voicings.name: Dadd9
voicings.fingering: Open D with open 1st string ringing
voicings.use: Bright, shimmery open voicing for ballads and pop

voicings.name: Eadd9
voicings.fingering: Open E shape with added 2nd fret on 1st string
voicings.use: Full, resonant voicing for rock and folk

voicings.name: Aadd9
voicings.fingering: Based on open A with pinky on 4th fret of 3rd string

voicingGroups.title: Barre & Movable Add Chord Shapes
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These movable shapes let you play add chords in any key up the neck. Learn the root-note shapes and slide them to the fret you need.

voicings.name: Fadd9
voicings.fingering: Partial barre F shape with 3rd fret on 4th string
voicings.use: Common in pop progressions with C and G

voicings.name: Bbadd9
voicings.fingering: Barre shape at 1st fret with add9 note

voicings.name: Em(add9)
voicings.fingering: Open Em with 2nd fret on 4th string lifted
voicings.use: Haunting minor color, great for ambient and indie

voicings.name: Am(add9)
voicings.fingering: Open Am shape with open 2nd string
voicings.use: Melancholy but shimmery, perfect for arpeggios

voicings.name: Dm(add9)
voicings.fingering: Open Dm with open 1st string ringing
voicings.use: Adds gentle dissonance to minor chord, singer-songwriter favorite

items.title: Wonderwall Pattern (Oasis Style)

strumming.description: Driving acoustic strum with add9 color

items.description: The iconic Oasis-style pattern built on add9 and sus voicings. The added 9th gives the major chords a wider, more emotional quality than plain triads.

items.title: Modern Pop Ballad
items.description: Replace every triad with its add9 version for a lush, shimmering pop sound. The 9th acts like a common tone linking the chords together smoothly.

items.title: U2 / Ambient Rock Pattern
items.description: Arpeggiated add9 chords with dotted-eighth delay create The Edge's signature wide, shimmering soundscape. Let all strings ring openly.

items.title: Coldplay / Worship Progression

strumming.description: Building dynamic strum, quiet to loud

items.description: A Coldplay-inspired progression where every chord includes the 9th. The open strings and added notes create a wash of harmonics that builds beautifully with dynamics.

techniqueItems: Keep common tones ringing when switching between add9 chords - the added 9th often stays the same
Practice lifting just one finger to convert standard open chords to their add9 versions
Use hybrid picking (pick + fingers) to bring out the added 9th note in arpeggios
Let open strings ring as much as possible - the beauty of add chords is in the sustained overtones
applicationItems: Replace any major chord with its add9 for instant sophistication without extra complexity
Pair add9 chords with delay and reverb effects for atmospheric, ambient textures
Use add9 chords in intros and outros to create a signature sound
Combine add9 with sus4 voicings for dynamic tension-and-release movement within a progression

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises progress from simple chord conversions to full add9 chord progressions with arpeggios and strumming patterns.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Triad to Add9 Conversion
exercises.content: Pattern: C - Cadd9 - C | G - Gadd9 - G | D - Dadd9 - D | Am - Am(add9) - Am
exercises.detail: Start with a standard open chord, add the 9th by adding or lifting one finger, then return. Repeat each pair 8 times before moving on. The goal is to make the add9 feel like a natural extension of the triad.
exercises.tip: Notice which finger moves for each conversion. For Cadd9, you lift the pinky off the 1st string. For Gadd9, you add a finger on the 1st string 3rd fret.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Add9 Arpeggio Picking
exercises.detail: Arpeggiate each add9 chord slowly, letting every note ring. Listen for the shimmer the 9th adds compared to the plain triad. Use thumb for bass strings (6-5-4) and fingers for treble (3-2-1).
exercises.tip: Record yourself playing the same arpeggio with and without the add9 note to hear the difference clearly.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Full Add9 Progression Workout
exercises.content: Play: Gadd9 (2 bars) - Cadd9 (2 bars) - Em(add9) (2 bars) - Dadd9 (2 bars). Repeat with strumming, then fingerpicking, then hybrid picking.
exercises.detail: This is the most common add9 progression in modern pop. Practice at 70 BPM first, then build to 100 BPM. Focus on smooth voice leading - identify the notes that stay the same between chord changes.
exercises.tip: In this progression, the note D appears in Gadd9, Dadd9, and can ring through Cadd9 and Em(add9). Use this as an anchor tone.

concepts.title: Creative Add Chord Techniques
items: Minor add9: Cm(add9) = C-Eb-G-D creates a bittersweet, Radiohead-style sound
Add11 voicings: Cadd11 = C-E-G-F, but beware of the b9 interval between 3rd and 11th
Stacked add chords: Layer add9 with sus4 for complex textures (e.g., Gadd9/sus4)
Drop D add chords: Open 6th string as bass pedal under add9 shapes for massive sound
Nashville number system: Use 'add9' notation to communicate these chords in sessions

concepts.title: Add Chords in Composition & Arranging
items: Voice leading: The 9th often acts as a common tone between I(add9) and V(add9)
Orchestration: In a band context, let the guitarist play add9 while keys play the triad to avoid mud
Capo magic: Capo 2 with Cadd9/Gadd9 shapes gives Dadd9/Aadd9 with open-string resonance
Recording: Double-track add9 voicings panned left/right for a massive stereo spread
Contrast: Alternate between add9 and plain triads across verse/chorus for dynamic shift

journeySection.title: Continue Your Chord Journey
journeySection.description: Now that you understand add chords, explore how they connect to other chord types. Add chords sit between simple triads and complex extended harmony.

links.title: Suspended Chords
links.description: Compare add chords with sus chords - both add color, but sus replaces the 3rd while add keeps it.

links.description: Take the next step from add chords into 9ths, 11ths, and 13ths that include the 7th.
